skill.name: deploying-to-production
skill.description: Guide agents through build checks, GitHub repository setup, code push, Vercel deployment, and deployment verification for web projects.
skill.summary: Deploy web projects through build validation, GitHub publishing, Vercel release, and live verification.
skill.author: ZhanlinCui

security_audit.summary: The single static finding is a false positive caused by an inline Markdown build command. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden malicious deployment intent was found in SKILL.md.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 22 is an inline Markdown command showing a standard npm build step, not Ruby or shell backtick execution by the skill. The file is prompt-only and contains no executable wrapper around this text.

content.value_statement: Production releases require careful build checks, repository setup, and live verification. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through GitHub and Vercel deployment steps.
actual_capabilities: Runs a project build command before deployment and blocks progress on build errors.
Guides GitHub repository creation or reuse decisions.
Pushes the selected codebase to the configured Git remote.
Deploys a GitHub-backed web project to Vercel.
Captures and verifies the live deployment URL.
limitations: Requires valid GitHub and Vercel access configured outside the skill.
Does not choose production settings, domains, or secrets automatically.
Can expose private code if repository visibility is chosen incorrectly.
Assumes the project uses an npm build workflow.

use_cases.title: Ship a Client Website
use_cases.description: Validate the build, create the repository, deploy to Vercel, and share a tested URL.

use_cases.title: Publish an Internal Tool
use_cases.description: Move a web app from local development to a GitHub-backed Vercel deployment.

use_cases.title: Standardize Release Handoff
use_cases.description: Give agents a repeatable checklist for build, source control, deployment, and verification.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Production Deploy
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy this app to production using the deploying-to-production skill. Run the build first, then create or reuse a GitHub repository, deploy to Vercel, and verify the URL.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Build Then Deploy
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare this project for a Vercel production release. If the build fails, diagnose the error, apply a focused fix, rerun the build, then continue with GitHub and Vercel deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Use an Existing Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy this repository to Vercel with a clear release trail. Confirm repository reuse, push the expected branch, capture the deployment URL, and report verification results.

prompt_templates.title: Security-Aware Release
prompt_templates.prompt: After reviewing uncommitted changes, deploy this web project. Keep repository visibility explicit, avoid committing secrets, push the chosen branch, deploy on Vercel, and verify the live page.

output_examples.input: Deploy my portfolio site to production.
output_examples.output: The build passed, the repository was published to GitHub, and the site was deployed to Vercel. The live URL was verified successfully.
The report identifies the failed build step, summarizes the cause, applies a focused fix, and continues only after a successful rebuild.

output_examples.input: Deploy this app but use the existing repository.
output_examples.output: The workflow reuses the confirmed repository, pushes the expected branch, deploys from GitHub to Vercel, and returns the verified deployment URL.

best_practices: Confirm repository visibility before pushing code to GitHub.
Check for secrets, local configuration files, and generated artifacts before deployment.
Verify the live URL after every deployment and record the result.
anti_patterns: Creating a new repository when the user requested an existing one.
Pushing private or secret files without review.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy directly from local files?
faq.answer: It guides a GitHub-backed Vercel deployment. The project is pushed to GitHub before Vercel deployment.

faq.question: Does it require Vercel credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. The agent needs access through the user's configured Vercel account or CLI session.

faq.question: Can it fix build errors?
faq.answer: It can diagnose and fix build errors when the surrounding project files provide enough context.

faq.question: Will it choose repository visibility?
faq.answer: No. Repository visibility should be confirmed before pushing code.

faq.question: Is it safe for private projects?
faq.answer: It can be used for private projects when repository visibility, secrets, and deployment permissions are reviewed first.

faq.question: Does it configure custom domains?
faq.answer: No. The workflow focuses on GitHub setup, Vercel deployment, and URL verification.
